refute.method: Each SAME re-read against both clauses. COPY (2002 7.1.2) and REPLACE (2002 7.1.3) rules attacked through the 2002-only debugging-line context: a COPY or REPLACE statement may itself be written on a debugging line, pseudo-text may contain debugging lines, and debugging lines become comments only AFTER all COPY and REPLACE processing. So every COPY/REPLACE general rule governs text and statements 2023 does not have (2023's transcription contains no debugging line, debugging indicator or DEBUGGING MODE at all: grep 'debugging line' in specs/ISO_COBOL_2023.md finds 0 hits). This is the same reach the reader itself accepted for 2002-GR-7.1.2.3-14 and -7. Probes in E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out/refute-p-07/ (run.log), pinned compiler E:/COBOL-wt/coderead85-tree-d/src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe, --copy lib. All citations checked: refute-p-07/cites.log (48 OK, 0 FAIL).

cases.reason: 2002 SR10 lets pseudo-text-2 contain debugging lines, so the produced text can contain a COPY statement on a debugging line; at REPLACE time that line is not yet a comment (6.2.7), so the prohibition reaches it. 2023 has no such text. Probe repl_d_copy.cob (pseudo-text-2 holds a D-line 'COPY RPIN.', no DEBUGGING MODE): --std 2002 compiles and prints MAIN with no diagnostic; --std 2023 rejects the D line. LEAD, beyond this rule: repl_copy.cob (same, no D line) compiles at BOTH editions and the produced COPY is processed (prints MAIN, FROMLIB), which looks contrary to §2023:7.2.4.4 GR9 itself; the 2023 KEPT verdict for GR-7.2.4.4-9 may be wrong and deserves a separate check.
